comparison_rule: an element is one instance row named by a detection, spelled <object>:<name> (colleague:<name> or interaction:<name>); the baseline identifies an element only when one of its pre-registered per-row assertions fails on that row; the probe identifies an element when a check finding's witness (dangling arrow+row, or equation+row) resolves to that row; unique = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings are discovery questions, recorded verbatim, never counted as detections.

baseline_rules.colleague-hub-declared: every colleague's `hub` resolves to a declared Mediator row
baseline_rules.interaction-parties-declared: every interaction's `speaker` and `listener` resolve to declared Colleague rows and are distinct
baseline_rules.interaction-dispatch-declared: every interaction's `dispatched_by` resolves to a declared Mediator row
baseline_rules.documented-route: every interaction's (speaker, listener) pair equals the pre-registered documented route
baseline_rules.not-asserted: no composition of two arrows (speaker;hub, listener;hub) and no specific mediator row identity: composing arrows is the modeling act under test, and a second declared mediator row is exactly the migration fault
